arithmetic.shared_cell: two organisms on a cell take income/2 = 1.0 each with income 2, so a mover nets 1.0 - 0.2 - 0.1211 = +0.68
arithmetic.if_income_were_zero: a mover would lose 0.2 + 0.1211*2/3 = 0.2807 per step, so its energy would fall 56 units over 200 steps
arithmetic.discriminator: energy rises or falls at the crossing; the recovered income says by how much the assumed 1.0 is wrong

fires.evidence: mean income taken at the crossing 0.2977 vs the assumed 1.0 (half of income 2)

silent.evidence: no income, no movement: recovered income max |x| = 7.22e-16 over 2880 samples

verdict.reason: at the crossing the organism takes 0.2977 per step, not the 1.0 that a shared cell would give; the arithmetic that predicts a crossing at 0.8 assumes an income the organism does not get

limitations: income is recovered from the energy drop, so it assumes the step cost is exactly 0.2 + move_cost*moved; EXP-39 supports that but it was measured without income
the trace does not report how many organisms share a cell, so the recovered income says "less than half a cell" without saying how the cell was split
one seed, one density (n=120 on 120 cells); the crossing of EXP-36 was measured with the same setup, so the comparison holds but nothing generalises
